body:
The maintainer gave a screenshot in chat on 2026-11-17. The image is not attached here. This is what it shows.

Reproduction, with a file that ships with the program:
1. Open `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj` (build 0.23.0 `ea97d63b`, machine Tormach 770MX + microARC 4, post Tormach PathPilot).
2. Select the operation "Flat A90" (type Slot, tool EM 1/4, source Stock).
3. Open the Heights tab.

The values on the tab:
- "Tilted plane (3+2)" is set. Tool axis A is 90.0°. Tool axis B is 0.0°. Plane origin X, Y and Z are 0.0000 in.
- Clearance Z: from Top of stock, offset 0.5000 in (= Z 0.87500).
- Top Z: from Top of stock, offset 0.0000 in (= Z 0.37500).
- Bottom Z: from Top of stock, offset -0.0150 in (= Z 0.36000).

What the viewport shows:
- The clearance plane ("Flat A90 · Clearance 0.8750") is a horizontal rectangle above the part.
- The top plane and the bottom plane are horizontal rectangles through the stock, near the top of the bar.
- All three planes are at right angles to the Z of the setup. No plane is at right angles to the tool axis at A 90°.

Expected for A 90°: the three planes stand on the side of the bar that the tool points at, at right angles to the turned tool axis.

The same check applies to "Flat A-90" and "Flat A180" of the same file.

Investigation result (read-only, from the code on main `3c3a58686`; nothing was built or run).

**Category: wrong output, not only a display defect. The priority is now `P1`.**

**Generation**
- `collect_job` (`crates/app/src/operation/job.rs:216`) resolves the heights through `resolve_height` (`crates/app/src/operation/heights.rs`). "Top of stock" is the maximum Z of the stock box in the setup frame. "Top of model" is the maximum Z of the part box.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:234-248` then subtracts only `frame.origin.z` from each height. It does not measure the stock along the turned tool axis.
- Slot, Pocket, Contour and Drill read the same height set. Bore and Thread were not read.
- The correct function is there: `OpFrame::height_z_local` (`crates/app/src/operation/frame.rs:223-248`). Only `crates/app/tests/opframe_seam.rs` calls it.
- Only the level cap of #2004 uses the tool axis (`stock_top_in_frame`).

**Preview and panel**
- `crates/ui/src/interact.rs:1276-1330` draws the planes at the setup Z, across the XY box of the stock. It does not read the tilt.
- The "(= Z ...)" text (`crates/ui/src/operations.rs:109-117`) shows the same setup Z.

**Why the example looks correct**
- The stock of `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj` is symmetric about the A axis (dy = dz = 19.05 mm). The stock top along Z and along the turned axis are the same value, 9.525 mm.
- Thus the golden `examples/first-4axis-part.nc` cannot show the defect.
- The tests in `crates/app/tests/tilt.rs` use fixed heights only. No test has a tilted operation with a reference height on an asymmetric stock.

**Test that proves it**
- Stock dy = 10, dz = 30, centred on the axis. A Slot with Tilted plane A = 90 and Top "From: Top of stock" + 0.
- Expected stock top along the tool axis: 5. The code on main gives 15, by this reading.

**Limit of this result**
- This is a reading of the code. The first step of the fix is that test, to confirm the reading.

Done means:
- A tilted (3+2) operation measures each reference height along its tool axis.
- The viewport planes and the "(= ...)" text use the same frame.
- The asymmetric-stock test pins it.

fix on issue/2389-tilt-heights-axis · PR #2418 · pinned by tilt_heights::a_slot_at_a90_reads_top_of_stock_along_the_tool_axis, tilt_heights::an_offset_bar_reads_its_own_side_at_a_minus_90_and_the_underside, tilt_heights::a_tilted_contour_sections_the_model_along_the_tool_axis · merges when reviewed. Generation side only (heights, section plane, area-controls plane); the viewport planes and the '(= Z ...)' echo are split out to #2416 (P3).
